subject: general
question: When was the Mines Act enacted in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1952**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mines Act, 1952, was enacted by the Government of India to regulate the working conditions in mines and ensure the safety, health, and welfare of workers employed in mines.
 
• The Act applies to all types of mines, including open-cast and underground mines, and lays down provisions for inspections, safety measures, and penalties for violations.
 
• It mandates the appointment of qualified managers and supervisors to oversee mining operations and ensure compliance with safety standards.
 
• The Act specifies working hours, conditions of employment, and provisions for the welfare of workers, including medical facilities, canteens, and sanitation.
 
• The Mines Act, 1952, is a crucial legislation aimed at improving the living and working conditions of miners, reducing workplace hazards, and preventing exploitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The primary acts governing mining in India are:**

 
 
• The Mines Act, 1952, focusing on health, safety, and working conditions.
 
• The Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 (MMDR Act), which regulates the development and control of minerals under Union control, alongside specific rules like the Offshore Areas Mineral (Development & Regulation) Act, 2002 for offshore operations.
 
• These foundational laws, supplemented by various rules and amendments (like the MMDR Amendment Acts of 1986, 1994, 2010), create the framework for India's mining sector.
